author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Retire one EmuCoreX library root without deleting its files
summary: Map the exact entries owned by a root, remove only its Android tree grant, refresh once, prove other roots and saves remain intact, and handle physical files later as a separate owner-controlled action.
heroAlt: PCSX2 Linux setup wizard showing a selected game directory that can be retired independently from emulator data

blocks.text: Unlink the root before making a filesystem decision

Removing a library root should change what EmuCoreX scans, not what exists on storage. First determine which visible entries resolve through that document tree. If a second root overlaps it, counts cannot be predicted until the overlap is removed. BIOS, memory cards, profiles, and emulator data should be outside the game root and must not be part of this maintenance action.
Do not use Android's Delete command while testing a root removal. A tree grant can be restored; deleted personal images may not be recoverable.

items: Exact visible root name, provider, and physical storage recorded.
List of titles, serials, and relative paths resolved through that root.
Proof that no selected parent or child root overlaps it.
Backups of favorites, profiles, and emulator data.
A second healthy root or test title for regression checking.
1. Close any running game and wait for scanning or metadata work to finish.
2. Open the library-folder manager and select the exact root from the ownership list.
3. Use the app's remove or revoke action; do not navigate into Android Files to delete content.
4. Run one refresh and compare disappeared entries with the ownership list.
5. Launch a title from another root and confirm its favorite and profile remain present.
6. Force-stop and reopen EmuCoreX to prove the retired tree is not silently re-added.
7. Browse the retired physical folder with Android Files and confirm its images still exist.
8. Only after acceptance should the owner separately archive, move, or delete physical files.

blocks.text: If no entries disappear, another selected root may still cover the same tree. If too many disappear, the removed root may have been a broad parent. Restore the grant before changing files, then redesign non-overlapping roots.
Expected result of a clean retirement
The observed entry delta should equal the recorded ownership list, while physical content and unrelated data remain stable.

items: Only titles assigned to the retired root become unavailable or disappear.
Physical game files remain present and keep their hashes.
Other roots still cold-boot after restart.
Profiles and memory cards remain available.
The retired root no longer appears as an active scan source.
Nothing changes: another parent or duplicate root still exposes the files.
Unrelated titles disappear: the root map was broader than expected.
Saves disappear with the root: emulator data was incorrectly stored under the game tree.
Folder itself vanishes in Files: a storage or deletion event occurred outside the intended unlink action.

blocks.text: Use Android's picker to select the same physical folder, approve the grant, and refresh once. Compare the restored entries with the ownership list before attempting a narrower retirement. Restore emulator-data backup only if durable data was actually stored inside the retired tree and changed.
Cloud and removable providers may retain placeholders

A provider can show names for offline content or remount the same card under a new URI. Verify physical availability and hashes separately; unlinking a provider view is not a promise about remote retention or card health.
